strapiBlog.title: Freehold vs Leasehold Properties in Dubai: What You Need to Know
strapiBlog.short_description: Understand freehold vs leasehold property in Dubai to make informed real estate investment decisions and choose ownership rights confidently.

data.text:
Dubai's property market offers two distinct ownership routes: freehold and leasehold. The difference is not just legal terminology. It determines whether the buyer owns the land or only the right to use it. Foreign nationals can buy freehold property in over 60 designated zones, and a 2025 ruling has added even more addresses to the Dubai freehold map.

This guide breaks down the difference between freehold vs leasehold in Dubai, where each applies, and the rights each ownership type carries.

Key Insights

  • Freehold property in Dubai gives the buyer full ownership of both the building and the land.
  • Leasehold property in Dubai grants the right to occupy and use the property for a fixed term, typically up to 99 years.
  • Foreign nationals can buy freehold property only in designated freehold zones in Dubai.
  • In January 2025, the Dubai Land Department (DLD) approved 457 plots along Sheikh Zayed Road (128 plots) and Al Jaddaf (329 plots) for leasehold-to-freehold conversion.
  • Leasehold-to-freehold conversion carries a fee of 30% of the property's market value based on Gross Floor Area, payable to the Dubai Land Department.
  • Properties valued at AED 2 million or above, whether freehold or recently converted to freehold, qualify the owner for the 10-year UAE Golden Visa.
     

What is a Freehold Property in Dubai?

Freehold property in Dubai means complete and permanent ownership of both the unit and the land it sits on. The owner receives a title deed registered with the Dubai Land Department, which carries no expiry, no renewal requirement, and no time restriction.

Freehold owners can sell, lease, mortgage, gift, or pass the property to heirs without seeking approval from any third party.

The framework was established by the 2002 Freehold Decree, issued by His Highness Sheikh Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum, which opened property ownership in Dubai to foreign nationals for the first time. Today, over 60 designated freehold areas across Dubai accept foreign ownership, including the city's most active investment districts. 

Zoya Ventures Real Estate's guide to purchasing freehold property in Dubai covers the full ownership framework in detail.

Where are Freehold Properties Located in Dubai?

Freehold zones cover both the city's prime districts and its accessible-entry communities. The most active include:

  • Waterfront and iconic: Palm Jumeirah, Dubai Marina, Downtown Dubai, Emaar Beachfront, Bluewaters Island, La Mer
  • Master-planned suburbs: Dubai Hills Estate, Arabian Ranches, DAMAC Hills, DAMAC Lagoons, Tilal Al Ghaf, The Valley
  • Urban core: Business Bay, Dubai Creek Harbour, Sobha Hartland
  • Accessible entry: Jumeirah Village Circle (JVC), Jumeirah Village Triangle (JVT), International City, Discovery Gardens, Dubai South, Arjan, Al Furjan.

To explore the complete list of Dubai’s freehold areas, you can read our detailed blog.
 

What is a Leasehold Property in Dubai?

Leasehold property in Dubai gives the buyer the right to occupy and use the property for a fixed period, typically up to 99 years. The buyer holds the lease, but the land remains the property of the original owner, usually the Dubai Government or a UAE national. At the end of the lease, ownership reverts to the landowner unless the lease is renewed or renegotiated.

Leasehold owners can occupy, sublet, and modify the property within the terms of the lease, but major alterations and structural changes typically require the landowner's consent. Periodic rent or service obligations may apply, depending on the lease terms.

Where are Leasehold Properties Located in Dubai?

Leasehold areas in Dubai are typically older, more established neighborhoods that fall outside the designated freehold zones. 

The most common include parts of Deira, Bur Dubai, Karama, Satwa, Oud Metha, Al Qusais, Al Muhaisnah, Al Rashidiya, Naif, and Hor Al Anz. These zones remain reserved for UAE and GCC nationals on a freehold basis, with foreign nationals limited to leasehold arrangements.

The key distinction comes down to control and time. Freehold properties offer permanent ownership with full control, supporting long-term capital appreciation, inheritance planning, and unrestricted use. 

In comparison, leasehold properties offer time-bound rights at typically lower entry costs, suited to buyers prioritizing location over land ownership.

Considering a freehold purchase in 2026? Browse properties for sale across Dubai's freehold zones.

Leasehold-to-Freehold Conversion in Dubai

The most significant change to Dubai's freehold framework since 2002 came on January 19, 2025, when the Dubai Land Department announced that 457 plots along Sheikh Zayed Road and in Al Jaddaf would become eligible for leasehold-to-freehold conversion. The new development opened two of Dubai's most central addresses to foreign ownership for the first time.

  • Sheikh Zayed Road: 128 plots between the Trade Centre Roundabout and the Dubai Water Canal are eligible for conversion.
  • Al Jaddaf: 329 plots across the waterfront district are eligible.
  • Eligibility: Open to private property owners of all nationalities.
  • Conversion fee: 30% of the property's market value, calculated based on Gross Floor Area.
  • Application: Submitted through the Dubai REST app.

Pros of Buying Freehold Property in Dubai

The case for buying freehold property in Dubai rests on five factors:

  • Full ownership of land and building: No expiry, no renewal, no third-party landowner.
  • Strong capital appreciation: Freehold zones consistently lead Dubai's secondary market on resale demand and price growth.
  • Inheritance and estate planning: Full transfer to heirs with no time restriction. Foreign owners are advised to register a will through the DIFC Wills Service Centre to align with home-country intentions.
  • Golden Visa pathway: Freehold properties valued at AED 2 million or above qualify the owner for the 10-year UAE Golden Visa.
  • Full control over modifications: Owners can renovate, restructure, or rebuild without external approval, subject only to community-level architectural rules.

Read more in our guide to tax benefits for foreign property buyers in Dubai.

Pros of Buying Leasehold Property in Dubai

Leasehold ownership in Dubai has its place, particularly for buyers prioritizing location over land ownership:

  • Lower entry pricing: Leasehold properties in central districts typically price below comparable freehold inventory.
  • Access to established neighborhoods: Many leasehold zones sit in long-established parts of Dubai with mature infrastructure, schools, retail, and healthcare access.
  • Long-term rights: 99-year leases provide ownership rights that extend beyond most buyers' practical use horizons.
  • Lower upfront capital outlay: Useful for buyers with shorter intended hold periods or those prioritizing rental yield over capital appreciation.
  • The trade-offs are clear: no land ownership, restricted right to make structural changes, ownership reverts at lease expiry unless renewed, and a narrower resale market compared to freehold zones.

What to Consider Before Choosing Freehold or Leasehold Property in Dubai

Several factors should shape the decision between freehold and leasehold in Dubai:

Hold Period and Exit Strategy

Buyers planning to hold the property for over 10 years, build a Dubai portfolio, or pass it on to heirs benefit most from freehold ownership. Buyers with a five-year or shorter horizon may find leasehold pricing competitive for rental yield generation.

Location Priority

If the preferred neighborhood is in a designated freehold zone, freehold is the natural choice. If the location is in an older, central district reserved for UAE nationals on freehold, leasehold is the available route.

Investment Strategy

Capital-growth-led investors typically gravitate toward freehold in established zones such as Downtown Dubai, Palm Jumeirah, and Dubai Marina. Yield-focused investors with shorter holds may find leasehold viable in central, high-demand locations.

Golden Visa and Residency

The 10-year Golden Visa requires the property to be freehold and valued at AED 2 million or above. Leasehold properties typically do not qualify unless converted to freehold under the 2025 DLD framework.

Want to discuss whether freehold or leasehold suits your purchase plan? Talk to a Zoya Ventures Real Estate advisor for a tailored shortlist.

How to Check if a Property is Freehold or Leasehold

The simplest way to verify ownership status is through the Dubai REST app, which lists every registered property in Dubai along with its ownership type, title deed status, and developer details. Owners can also request a verification report from DLD or through a RERA-registered brokerage.

For buyers evaluating an off-plan purchase, the developer's RERA registration document and project listing on Dubai REST will indicate whether the project sits in a freehold zone.

faqs.question: Can foreigners buy freehold property in Dubai?

data.answer: Yes, since 2002, foreign nationals have been permitted to buy freehold property in Dubai's designated freehold zones.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a 99-year lease and freehold in Dubai?

data.answer: A 99-year lease grants the right to occupy and use a property for 99 years, with the land remaining under the original owner. Freehold grants permanent ownership of both the property and the land.

faqs.question: Can a leasehold property in Dubai be converted to freehold?

data.answer: Yes, in specific cases, the Dubai Land Department has allowed 457 plots along Sheikh Zayed Road and in Al Jaddaf to convert from leasehold to freehold status, subject to a 30% conversion fee.

faqs.question: Does freehold property in Dubai qualify for the Golden Visa?

data.answer: Yes, freehold property valued at AED 2 million or above qualifies the owner for the 10-year UAE Golden Visa.

faqs.question: Are there any restrictions on what foreigners can do with freehold property in Dubai?

data.answer: No, freehold property owners in Dubai have full rights to sell, lease, mortgage, renovate, gift or inherit the property.

faqs.question: Is leasehold property in Dubai cheaper than freehold?

data.answer: Generally, yes. Leasehold properties in older central districts typically price below compared to freehold inventory.

faqs.question: What happens to a leasehold property at the end of the lease?

data.answer: At the end of the lease term, ownership reverts to the original landowner unless the lease is renewed or renegotiated.

faqs.question: Can joint owners hold a freehold property in Dubai?

data.answer: Yes, joint ownership of freehold property is permitted under DLD regulations, with each owner's share registered on the title deed. Our guide to joint property ownership in Dubai covers the structure in detail.

faqs.question: How do I verify whether a property is freehold or leasehold?

data.answer: The Dubai REST app, available through DLD, allows users to verify the ownership status of any registered property in Dubai.
